one_liner: SIMD multithreaded ETC1/ETC2/EAC/BC encoder: 500-1400x faster than Etc2Comp/ETCPACK multithreaded, 9-21x single-thread scalar, at lower quality.
what_it_does: Compresses PNG images into GPU block-compressed textures (ETC1, ETC2 RGB/RGBA, EAC R11/RG11, BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC7) and writes PVR or DDS files, with optional mipmaps and dithering; it also decodes those formats back to PNG. The shipped product is a command-line tool (CMake builds only an `etcpak` executable). Embedders copy the encoder files instead: per-format functions such as `CompressEtc2Rgb(const uint32_t* src, uint64_t* dst, uint32_t blocks, size_t width, bool useHeuristics)` take a raw 32-bit pixel buffer and write 64-bit blocks. Godot vendors exactly these files (Process*.cpp plus Tables, Dither, Math, Vector).
how_it_is_fast: The ETC1 path does no endpoint search. It averages the block's colour for both 2x4/4x2 sub-block splits, keeps the split with the lowest error, then picks the best intensity-modifier table and selectors with SSE4.1/AVX2/NEON error arithmetic. Solid blocks exit early. ETC2 adds the QuickETC2 scheme (Nah, ACM TOG 2020; shipped in etcpak 1.0 as 'heuristics'): a luma-range test sends very-low-contrast blocks straight to planar mode (thresholds 0.03/0.09/0.38 in ProcessRGB.cpp). Only high-contrast blocks go to a luma-ordered T/H-mode search. BC1 takes per-channel bounding-box min/max endpoints with an inset and assigns selectors by projecting the summed channel offsets, all in SSE/AVX/NEON registers. BC7 is a SIMD-rewritten copy of Rich Geldreich's bc7enc (AVX2/AVX-512 paths). Images are cut into 32-block-row slices on a thread pool.
when_to_use: Development or iteration builds that have to re-encode many or very large textures (8K-16K atlases) to ETC1/ETC2 in seconds rather than hours
Runtime or on-device texture encoding where a few ms per 4K texture matters more than about 1 dB of PSNR (Godot uses it for its in-engine ETC/BC compression)
Producing ETC2 for OpenGL ES 3 / Android targets when Etc2Comp at effort 0 or ETCPACK is the current bottleneck
Fast BC1/BC3/BC4/BC5 encoding on x86-64 or AArch64 when quality is checked by eye rather than by a PSNR target
when_not_to_use: Final shipping assets where quality matters: in the QuickETC2 paper the etcpak-derived ETC2 is 0.72-1.47 dB PSNR below Etc2Comp and ETCPACK, and the paper names etcpak's ETC1 logic as the cause. Open issues report artefacts on subtle blue/white shades (#48) and over-brightened output (#40)

Colour gradients whose channels move in opposite directions (for example red to green) in BC1: endpoints are the bounding-box min/max corners, with no PCA or cluster fit, so the encoder cannot represent that axis (from reading ProcessDxtc.cpp)
Needs it does not cover: ETC2 RGB with punch-through alpha (open issue #21), ASTC, KTX/KTX2 output, or input formats other than PNG

Portable binaries: SIMD is chosen at compile time and CMake defaults to -march=native with no runtime dispatch, so a binary built on a new CPU can crash with an illegal instruction on an older one (issue #39, SSSE3 shuffle on an Athlon II)
High-quality BC7: the BC7 encoder is bc7enc limited to modes 1/6 (RGB) and 5/6/7 (RGBA), and the README's BC7 speed (12.1 Mpx/s single-threaded on a 7950X) has no competitor timing

integration.form: source-drop (the repo builds only a CLI executable; copy ProcessRGB/ProcessDxtc, Tables, Dither, Math, Vector, ForceInline and ProcessCommon, plus bc7enc.cpp for BC7)
integration.dependencies: Encoder files: none beyond the C++ standard library. CLI: libpng via pkg-config, and Tracy fetched from its master branch by CPM at configure time (network needed). BC7 decode uses the bundled bcdec.h (MIT)
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.29 and C++20 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20; bc7enc.cpp includes <bit>); GCC/Clang/MSVC paths are present, but SIMD on MSVC depends on __SSE4_1__/__AVX2__ being defined (since July 2026 __AVX__ implies SSE4.1)
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE4.1, AVX2, AVX-512 paths), AArch64 NEON (ARMv7 NEON fixed per issue #25), scalar fallback; SIMD level fixed at compile time
integration.thread_safety: Compress* functions work on caller buffers and only read shared tables, so different slices can be encoded in parallel. bc7enc_compress_block_init() must run once before BC7 use, and the bundled TaskDispatch pool is a process-wide singleton.

gotchas: --disable-heuristics does more than turn off the mode shortcut: in ProcessRGB_ETC2 the T/H-mode search runs only inside the heuristics branch. Without it, ETC2 output is limited to ETC1, planar and solid blocks.

Width and height must be multiples of 4. This is checked only by assert() in BlockData and Bitmap, so release builds do not reject other sizes. The CLI's PNG loader also ignores setjmp's return value, so a libpng error does not abort cleanly.

Licence hygiene: LICENSE.txt is BSD-3 but keeps template placeholders ('<organization>', '<COPYRIGHT HOLDER>'; open issue #24). ProcessRGB.cpp holds T/H helper functions marked '(C) Ericsson AB 2005-2013. All Rights Reserved' from ETCPACK v2.74, which point to an Ericsson statement the file does not include.
Channel order is easy to get wrong: ETC paths expect BGRA-ordered input while BC paths expect RGBA (Application.cpp sets bgr only for ETC codecs; issues #32 and #34 complain about the naming).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick etcpak over Goofy (ETC1/DXT1 only) when you need full ETC2 (planar, T and H modes, EAC alpha), BC3-BC5 or mipmapped PVR/DDS output from one tool. Pick bc7enc or bc7e directly for BC7 quality control, and ICBC for higher-quality BC1. Basis Universal's etc1f only claims, with no numbers, to be faster than etcpak.
verified_claims_summary: The independent QuickETC2 paper (ACM TOG 39(6), 2020; Ryzen 7 3700X, Ubuntu 20.04, compiler and flags not stated) timed etcpak 0.7 on 55 RGB textures. ETC2 planar-only ran at 1931 Mpx/s with 16 threads and SIMD (28.9 Mpx/s single-threaded scalar) against Etc2Comp effort 0 at 3.8 (3.1) and single-threaded ETCPACK 4.0.1 at 1.4 Mpx/s, at 36.82 dB vs 37.89/38.09 dB PSNR. Today's etcpak (1.0 and later) ships the paper's QuickETC2 T/H-mode and early mode-decision code, whose row in the same table is 2577 Mpx/s (40.6 single-threaded scalar) at 37.17 dB. The README's own Ryzen 9 7950X numbers (for example ETC2 356 Mpx/s single-threaded) time no competitor.
status_note: Actively maintained by Tracy's author (release 2.1 in February 2026, last commit 2026-09-13), BSD-3 and vendored by Godot; its 11 open issues are mostly quality and API complaints with no maintainer replies.
